purpose: Machine-readable legal framework for screening listed Korean companies for activist vulnerability, minority-shareholder leverage, governance risk and potential value-unlock opportunities.
important_note: This is an investment-research ruleset, not legal advice. A rule being potentially relevant to a company does not mean the company or its directors have breached the law. Company-specific legal conclusions require fact-specific analysis and, where appropriate, Korean counsel.

rules.statutory_summary: Directors must faithfully perform their duties for the company and shareholders, protect the interests of all shareholders, and treat the interests of all shareholders fairly.
rules.activist_relevance: Creates a stronger statutory basis for scrutinising board decisions where controller or affiliated interests may diverge from the interests of minority shareholders.
screening_flags: transaction disproportionately benefits controller or affiliate
minority shareholders bear dilution or economic disadvantage
board rationale for unequal treatment appears weak

scoring_use.note: Do not award points merely for low ROE or poor performance. Award only where a disclosed board action raises a plausible controller/minority conflict or fair-treatment issue.

rules.statutory_summary: Treasury shares do not carry ordinary shareholder rights including voting and dividend rights, and the 2026 reform further restricts their use.
rules.activist_relevance: Treasury shares should not be treated as controller voting stock when calculating AGM arithmetic, and large treasury positions can create per-share value-unlock potential if cancelled.
screening_flags: treasury shares historically used in control-related transactions
treasury shares materially depress per-share ownership

rules.statutory_summary: Treasury shares acquired after the reform must in principle be cancelled within one year of acquisition. Specified exceptions allow retention or disposal if the company prepares a treasury-share retention/disposal plan and obtains shareholder approval.
rules.transition_rule: Treasury shares acquired before the law took effect are, according to the Ministry of Justice's official reform explanation, subject in principle to an 18-month cancellation period.
exceptions_summary: employee or executive compensation including stock-option-related use
certain management-purpose uses where the articles contain the ground following the required shareholder resolution
rules.activist_relevance: Creates a concrete campaign route at companies with large legacy treasury holdings: demand cancellation, challenge weak retention rationales, and vote on retention/disposal plans.
screening_flags: large treasury shares relative to market cap
retention plan relying on vague management-purpose rationale
prior attempts to transfer treasury shares to friendly parties

rules.practical_summary: A shareholder continuously holding at least 1.5% for six months may exercise the listed-company special minority rights corresponding to Article 366 and Article 467, including the extraordinary-general-meeting route.
rules.activist_relevance: Sets a measurable entry cost for forcing an EGM-related process at a listed company.

rules.practical_summary: Qualifying shareholders may submit shareholder proposals under the listed-company special threshold.
rules.activist_relevance: Core route for putting director nominees, dividends, governance amendments and other permitted proposals on the AGM agenda.

rules.practical_summary: The listed-company special rule lowers the ownership threshold for specified removal-related shareholder rights.
rules.activist_relevance: Potential escalation tool in serious director or auditor misconduct disputes; not a routine governance campaign mechanism.

rules.practical_summary: Qualifying shareholders can invoke the listed-company special threshold for inspection/copying rights associated with accounting books and records.
rules.activist_relevance: Potentially powerful investigative route where an activist suspects related-party transactions, misuse of assets or other governance problems.

rules.practical_summary: Qualifying listed-company shareholders can access the lower statutory threshold for the Article 402 injunction route.
rules.activist_relevance: Could become relevant where a board is about to take an allegedly unlawful action that may cause irreparable company harm.

rules.practical_summary: A shareholder continuously holding at least 0.01% for six months may use the listed-company special threshold for a shareholder derivative action.
rules.activist_relevance: Very low economic ownership threshold makes litigation pressure feasible even without a large voting stake, although standing and merits remain separate questions.

rules.practical_summary: The listed-company special rule provides a 0.5% six-month threshold for the multiple-derivative-action right under Article 406-2.
rules.activist_relevance: Potentially relevant in holding-company and parent/subsidiary structures where alleged misconduct occurs at a subsidiary.

rules.applies_to: listed companies in the asset-size category specified by Presidential Decree; official Ministry of Justice summary identifies the reform target as large listed companies with total assets of at least KRW 2 trillion
rules.request_deadline: 6 weeks before the shareholder meeting under the listed-company special rule
rules.statutory_change: For companies subject to Article 542-7(2), the articles may no longer exclude cumulative voting.
rules.activist_relevance: Potentially allows a minority coalition to concentrate votes and elect at least one director even where it cannot win an ordinary majority vote.

rules.statutory_summary: Listed companies generally must have independent directors comprising at least one-third of the board, subject to statutory/decree exceptions. Larger listed companies in the specified category must have at least three independent directors and a majority-independent board.
rules.activist_relevance: Creates a baseline against which nominal and substantive board independence can be measured.
screening_flags: prior employment or business ties to controller

rules.applies_to: listed companies subject to the audit-committee provision
rules.statutory_summary: For election or removal of audit-committee members, voting rights above 3% are restricted. For the largest shareholder, holdings of specified related persons are aggregated for purposes of the cap.
rules.activist_relevance: Can dramatically reduce a controller's effective voting advantage in audit-committee contests.

rules.applies_to: listed companies subject to the relevant audit-committee requirements
rules.statutory_change: The 2025 second Commercial Act reform expands the number of audit-committee-member directors required to be elected separately from one to two.
rules.activist_relevance: Creates additional board-entry opportunities where the controller's voting power is constrained by the audit-committee election rules.
rules.verification_note: Included on the basis of the Ministry of Justice's official reform summary. Re-check the consolidated effective statutory text after 2026-09-10 before automated company scoring.

scoring_framework_v1.overall_score_note: Do not use a simple average initially. Keep component scores visible and develop the weighting only after testing against real companies and historical campaigns.
